text: The 2021–22 Premier League marked the 30th season of the league since its founding in 1992 and the 123rd season of top-flight English football. The season began on 25 March 2021 and ended on 30 May 2022, with fixtures released on 16 June 2021. Manchester City defended their title for the second consecutive year, winning their sixth Premier League title and eighth English league title overall, making it their fourth title in the last five seasons. They were the defending champions, having won the previous season's title. The season featured full attendance after the restrictions of the COVID-19 pandemic, which had limited or halted matches in the final third of 2019–20 and the entire 2020–21 season. It also included a winter break with no matches scheduled between 23 January and 7 February 2022. The early title race was led by Liverpool, Manchester City, and Chelsea, who were within two points of each other by early December. Chelsea led briefly after a run of 14 unbeaten matches until a defeat to West Ham United gave City the advantage. City then won 12 consecutive games, including a victory over Chelsea, building a 13-point lead by January (though Liverpool had two games in hand due to COVID-19 postponements). Liverpool responded with a 10-game winning streak, including their games in hand, and a 2–3 home loss to Tottenham Hotspur in February reduced City's lead to one point before their match on 10 April. A 2–2 draw preserved City's narrow lead. On 7 October, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund acquired an 80% stake in Newcastle United for £300 million, ending Mike Ashley's 14-year ownership. An emergency meeting on 12 October involving the other 19 clubs expressed anger over the takeover, with Newcastle excluded from the meeting. On 18 November, clubs voted to tighten financial controls to limit Newcastle's spending. At the time of the takeover, Newcastle were in 19th place after failing to win any of their first seven games; Steve Bruce was dismissed and Eddie Howe appointed. Newcastle did not win until their 15th match, but after five January signings, they won 12 of their final 18 games to finish 11th. In December, multiple matches were postponed due to COVID-19 outbreaks, with clubs calling for a league shutdown; a meeting on 20 December led to fixtures being played over Christmas if safe, with clubs advised to play if they had 13 fit players plus a goalkeeper. On 2 March, Roman Abramovich announced plans to sell Chelsea, intending to donate all proceeds to Ukraine victims of the Russian invasion. Reports followed of interest from Hansjörg Wyss, Todd Boehly, Javed Afridi, and others. On 10 March, the UK government froze Abramovich's assets due to his ties with Vladimir Putin, halting Chelsea's ability to sell tickets, merchandise, or players, and negotiate contracts. A government licence allowed football operations, employee payments, and season-ticket access. For the first time in Premier League history, all title, Champions League, Europa League, Conference League qualifications, and relegation battles were decided on the final day. With a one-point lead over Liverpool, Manchester City needed to match or exceed Liverpool's result to secure back-to-back titles; Liverpool needed a win and hope City lost to Aston Villa, managed by Steven Gerrard. Liverpool fell behind Wolves early but equalised; Aston Villa took a 2–0 lead after 63 minutes via goals from Matty Cash and Philippe Coutinho. Manchester City scored three goals in under six minutes (Ilkay Gundogan and Rodri as substitutes) to take the lead. Liverpool responded with late goals from Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson to win 3–1, but the result was irrelevant as City won 3–2 against Villa to claim their fourth title in five seasons. The season is remembered for the high quality of play by Manchester City and Liverpool, resulting in a fierce title race similar to the 2018–19 season, but also for VAR issues in its third season in England, including a high intervention threshold that led to few decisions, such as the failure to award a penalty in the Everton–Manchester City match due to a handball by Rodri, which impacted the title race. Norwich City, promoted from the Championship, were relegated with four games to spare after a 10th loss in 12 matches, recording the worst goal difference since Derby County in 2007–08. Watford, also promoted, were the second team to be relegated after a defeat to Crystal Palace. The final relegation spot was contested by Everton, Burnley, and Leeds United, all of whom struggled in the final months. Everton won only three games between October and April, but victories over Manchester United, Chelsea, and Leicester City meant a 3–2 win over Crystal Palace in their final home game secured safety; Dominic Calvert-Lewin's 85th-minute goal led to fans storming the pitch. Fans again invaded the pitch at full time after avoiding relegation since 1951, extending their top-flight status to 69 years. Burnley and Leeds were level on 35 points, with Burnley having a better goal difference. Burnley fell behind 2–0 to Newcastle, while Raphinha scored a penalty to put Leeds ahead against Brentford in the 54th minute. A 78th-minute equaliser from Brentford and a Maxwel Cornet goal gave Burnley hope, but Jack Harrison's added-time goal confirmed Leeds' safety and relegated Burnley after six consecutive seasons in the Premier League. Chelsea secured a top-four finish for the fourth consecutive season, leaving only Tottenham and Arsenal in contention for the Champions League spot. Arsenal were in 4th with three games left, but losses to Tottenham in the North London derby and to Newcastle in their final away game, combined with Tottenham's win over Burnley, saw them fall behind. Spurs needed only a point against already relegated Norwich to qualify for the first time in three years and won 5–0, with Son Heung-min scoring two goals to share the Golden Boot with Mohamed Salah. Arsenal failed to qualify for the Champions League for the sixth season despite a 5–1 win over Everton. Manchester United had a difficult season, culminating in the sacking of Ole Gunnar Solskjær on 21 November 2021 after a 4–1 loss to Watford; Ralf Rangnick took over as interim manager. The club finished 6th with a zero goal difference and the worst points total in the Premier League era at 58, losing on the final day. They qualified for the Europa League, but not back-to-back spots, as West Ham's 3–1 defeat at Brighton meant they settled for the Europa Conference League. Brentford manager Thomas Frank had a strong first season, aided by the January signing of Christian Eriksen, winning seven of their last 11 games, including a 4–1 win over Chelsea. The team finished 13th, 11 points above the relegation zone and never spent a week in the bottom half. Brighton had their best top-flight season under Graham Potter, finishing ninth with 51 points despite a poor home record; their 4–0 win over Manchester United was their biggest top-flight victory. Twenty teams competed: the top 17 from the previous season and three promoted from the Championship—Norwich City, Watford, and Brentford. These replaced Fulham, West Bromwich Albion, and Sheffield United, all of whom were relegated after brief top-flight spells. Brentford's return marked their first season in the Premier League after a 74-year absence. Four players scored four goals: one for the home team, one for the away team.
